question.text: A mutual fund distributor creates a social media post about an equity fund that has existed for more than three years, stating: "Invest in XYZ Equity Fund — it has given 45% returns in the last 6 months! Guaranteed to double your money in 2 years!" Which SEBI Advertisement Code violations are present in this post?

answer.text: Only the guarantee claim violates the code; showing 6-month returns is acceptable
Only showing past performance for a non-standard period is a violation
Multiple violations: (1) guarantee/assured returns claim, (2) non-standard performance period (6 months instead of 1/3/5 years), (3) no mandatory risk disclaimer, (4) no benchmark comparison
There are no violations as distributors are exempt from the Advertisement Code

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series V-A workbook (p84-p86), guaranteeing or assured-return language is prohibited, performance must be shown for standardised periods with the prescribed risk disclaimer and benchmark, and distributor advertising is covered by the Advertisement Code (p252, p306). For a scheme that has existed for more than three years, a stand-alone 6-month return is not a standardised period, so the post breaches the performance-period rule in addition to the guarantee, disclaimer and benchmark requirements. The Trap: Option D wrongly suggests distributors are exempt from the Advertisement Code; p252 and p306 make clear they are not. Identifying only a single violation misses the cumulative breach pattern (guarantee + period + disclaimer + benchmark). Note: Page 86 permits a 6-month performance disclosure for schemes older than six months but less than one year; the stem here is a 3-year-plus scheme, so the standardised 1/3/5-year (and since-inception) framework applies and a 6-month figure is not standardised.
